papers.title: Collective Responsibility and Individual Compensation
papers.title_ja: 集団的責任と個人の補償
summary_ja: 個人、集団、および環境要因が結果に影響する状況下での分配的正義を分析する。
集団間と集団内の二段階で資源配分を行う二つのルールを提案し、公理的特徴付けを行う。
Fleurbaeyの自然な報酬と補償の原理を、集団的責任が存在する枠組みへと拡張した。
papers.reason_ja: 責任の所在を考慮した分配的正義の公理的アプローチに関心がある方に最適です。
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes distributive justice in the presence of collective responsibility. We consider a society partitioned into groups, where three types of characteristics affect individual outcomes: circumstances for which neither individuals nor groups are responsible, collective responsible factors for which groups, but not individuals, bear responsibility, and personal responsible factors for which individuals are responsible. We propose two allocation rules: (i) group conditional equality and (ii) group egalitarian equivalence. Both solutions use a two-step procedure in which inter-group resource allocation is determined, and intra-group distribution second. This approach respects both individual agency within groups and collective responsibility across groups. We examine the basic properties of these allocation rules and offer axiomatic characterizations of them. For the characterizations, we extend the classical principles of natural reward and compensation developed by Marc Fleurbaey to the collective responsibility setting.

papers.title: Periodic Equity Prioritarianism
papers.title_ja: 期間的公平プライオリタリアニズム
summary_ja: 時間を通じて個人の厚生が異なる状況におけるプライオリタリアニズムのあり方を検討する。
リスク下の社会的評価における緊張を解消する手法を応用し、新たな評価基準を提案する。
本手法は、タイムスライス型および生涯型のプライオリタリアニズムが抱える問題を回避する。
papers.reason_ja: 時間軸を考慮した厚生評価やプライオリタリアニズムの理論的進展に関心がある方へ。
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper engages with the question of how to understand prioritarianism when people are differently well off at different times. In this context, it introduces a new version of prioritarianism, periodic equity prioritarianism , which is inspired by how focusing on equally distributed equivalents can dissolve tensions in social evaluations that involve risk. The paper shows that periodic equity prioritarianism avoids both certain problems that timeslice prioritarianism faces and some problems that lifetime prioritarianism faces.

papers.title: Obvious Group Manipulations and Top Trading Cycles
papers.title_ja: 集団による明白な操作とトップ・トレーディング・サイクル
summary_ja: Troyan and Morrillが定義した非明白な操作可能性を集団版へと拡張し、その性質を分析する。
この新たな条件が集団戦略耐性よりも弱く、従来の定義よりも強いことを示す。
Shapley-Scarf住宅市場において、トップ・トレーディング・サイクル（TTC）メカニズムを特徴付ける。
papers.reason_ja: マッチング理論における戦略的操作可能性とメカニズム設計に関心がある方へ。
papers.abstract: We introduce a group version of non-obvious manipulability, which is stronger than the original definition by Troyan and Morrill (2020) and weaker than group strategy-proofness, and study its implications in Shapley-Scarf housing markets. We provide several characterizations of the Top Trading Cycles mechanism using the new condition.

papers.title: Bimodal spread majorization: bridging inequality, bipolarization, and polarization in income tax policy
papers.title_ja: 双峰的広がりメジャライゼーション：所得税政策における不平等、二極化、分極化の架け橋
summary_ja: 所得税政策の文脈において、不平等や二極化、分極化を評価する指標を提案していると推測される。
双峰的広がりメジャライゼーション（Bimodal spread majorization）という概念を用い、所得分布の変容を分析する枠組みを提供している可能性がある。
税制が所得分布の形状に与える影響を、統計的な広がりと分布の偏りの観点から評価する手法を提示していると見られる。
papers.reason_ja: 所得税政策の評価指標や分布の分極化分析に関心がある研究者におすすめです。

papers.title: On dynamic income taxation and absolute inequality
papers.title_ja: 動的所得税制と絶対的不平等について
summary_ja: 動的な所得税制の設計において、絶対的不平等の指標をどのように扱うかを検討していると推測される。
時間経過に伴う所得の変動と税負担の関係を、絶対的不平等の観点から理論的に分析している可能性がある。
動的最適課税の枠組みにおいて、不平等の尺度を絶対的な基準で評価することの含意を考察していると見られる。
papers.reason_ja: 動的最適課税理論と不平等尺度の関係を深く掘り下げたい研究者におすすめです。

papers.title: Poverty-reducing taxation with endogenous income
papers.title_ja: 内生的な所得を伴う貧困削減のための課税（推測）
summary_ja: 所得が内生的に決定される経済モデルにおいて、貧困削減を目的とした最適な課税政策を分析している可能性がある。
所得水準が税制や再分配政策に依存して変化する状況下での、社会厚生最大化や貧困緩和の条件を考察していると推測される。
社会選択理論の枠組みにおいて、所得分布の変容を考慮した税制設計の理論的帰結を導出している可能性がある。
papers.reason_ja: 内生的な所得変化を考慮した税制設計の理論的分析に関心がある方へ。

papers.title: Motor precision shapes information seeking in perceptual decisions
papers.title_ja: 知覚的意思決定における運動精度と情報探索の関係
summary_ja: 知覚的判断に伴う運動コストが、意思決定の確信度（confidence）および情報探索行動に与える影響を実験的に検証した。
運動コストが低い反応は確信度の低下と関連し、その結果として追加的な情報探索を促す傾向があることを示した。
知覚的正確性に変化はないものの、運動コストが確信度を介して意思決定後の行動を調整する機能的役割を果たすと結論づけた。
papers.reason_ja: 意思決定における確信度と情報探索のメカニズムに関心がある方へ。
papers.abstract: Adaptive behavior relies heavily on the confidence we have in our decisions. For instance, in the absence of explicit feedback, the confidence associated with a decision determines whether we seek additional evidence or are likely to change our mind. Recent studies suggest that confidence estimation also depends on motor processes involved in implementing perceptual decisions. However, whether motor-induced changes in confidence meaningfully affect behavior, such as by altering information-seeking, remains uncertain. The present study addresses this question. Participants performed a perceptual task requiring discrimination of the orientation of Gabor patches. The motor cost of the perceptual response was manipulated by varying the size of the response circles that participants had to reach to report their judgment. Consistent with previous findings showing that easier motor responses are associated with lower confidence ratings, we found that such responses were also linked to a greater tendency to seek additional evidence compared to more costly responses. Importantly, this increase in information-seeking behavior was not accompanied by any change in perceptual accuracy. These findings support the idea that the motor costs associated with perceptual decisions modulate confidence, and that such motor-induced changes in confidence play a functional role in guiding subsequent behavior.

papers.title: Obvious group manipulations in voting
papers.title_ja: 投票における明白な集団操作
summary_ja: 連合の選択肢集合のみから識別可能な「明白な集団操作（obvious group manipulation）」の概念を定義し分析した。
トップのみ（tops-only）ルールやコンドルセ整合的なルールにおいて、この操作不可能性（NOMG）が独裁制と密接に関連することを示した。
特定の投票者数や選択肢数の条件下で、NOMGを満たすルールの限界やボルダ・ルール等の性質を詳細に特徴づけた。
papers.reason_ja: 投票ルールの戦略的操作不可能性に関する最新の理論的進展に関心がある方へ。
papers.abstract: We study obvious group manipulation in voting and characterize it as manipulation identifiable from a coalition's option sets alone. Our analysis focuses on two overlapping classes: tops-only rules and rules satisfying the majority criterion, including all Condorcet-consistent rules. On the universal domain with at least three alternatives, a tops-only rule is not obviously manipulable by groups (NOMG) if and only if it is dictatorial. For rules satisfying the majority criterion, NOMG is impossible when $n,m\geq3$, except with four voters and three alternatives. We quantify the coalition sizes behind these restrictions, obtaining sharp bounds for efficient tops-only rules and an exact threshold for majority-criterion rules with odd electorates. In the exceptional configuration, we characterize an interval of NOMG scoring rules containing Borda, which is also Condorcet consistent there. We further characterize NOMG with two alternatives and apply our tops-only characterization to generalized median voter schemes and voting by committees.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of Koray's Theorem
summary_ja: 中立的かつ全会一致な社会的選択関数が普遍的に自己選択的（universally self-selective）であるための必要十分条件が独裁制であることを示す定理を再証明した。
従来の証明がアローの不可能性定理に依拠していたのに対し、循環的な選好プロファイルを構築する直接的な手法を提案した。
有限の選択肢集合において、選ばれた選択肢を最上位に置く投票者が独裁者であることを示す簡潔な論理構成を提供している。
papers.reason_ja: 社会的選択関数の自己選択性と独裁制に関する理論的基礎を再確認したい方へ。
papers.abstract: In this note, I provide a direct and self-contained proof of Koray's (2000) theorem, by which a neutral and unanimous social choice function is universally self-selective if and only if it is dictatorial. Koray's (2000) original proof relies on results by Sen (1970) and Houthakker (1950) to construct a social welfare function for each alternative set. He then shows that these functions are Paretian and independent of irrelevant alternatives, allowing him to apply Arrow's (1950, 1951) impossibility theorem. Instead, I construct a cyclic preference profile and show that the voter who ranks the chosen alternative first is the dictator on every finite nonempty alternative set.

papers.title: Reasoning about risk and the Sure-thing Postulate
papers.title_ja: リスクに関する推論と確実性公理
summary_ja: サヴェッジの意思決定モデルにおける「確実性公理（Sure-thing Postulate）」が、宝くじに含まれる重要な情報を無視していると批判した。
最頻値や中央値といった宝くじの統計的性質が、合理的な選択の根拠となり得ることを指摘した。
これらの統計的性質と確実性公理が対立する事例を提示し、主観的期待効用理論およびベイズ的確率論の論理的基盤を再考している。
papers.reason_ja: 期待効用理論の公理的基礎と意思決定の合理性に関する哲学的議論に関心がある方へ。
papers.abstract: Savage’s normative model of rational decision-making is deficient because the Sure-thing Postulate systematically ignores important information contained in lotteries. Useful statistical facts about lotteries, such as their modes and medians, are available as defeasible reasons for reasoned choices between lotteries. Because such summary statistics are holistic properties of lotteries, we can find cases where appealing to facts about modes and medians as normative reasons for choosing between lotteries conflicts with Savage’s Sure-thing Postulate. Such cases show the Sure-thing Postulate to be implausible and undermine both Savage’s argument for subjective expected utility theory and his argument for Bayesian subjective probabilism.

papers.title: An axiomatic foundation for optimized certainty equivalents
papers.title_ja: 最適化された確実性等価（OCE）の公理的基礎
summary_ja: 平均分散基準や期待ショートフォールを含むリスク尺度である最適化された確実性等価（OCE）を公理的に特徴付けた。
「公正コイン補償」という新たな公理を導入し、強リスク回避性や正規化と組み合わせることでOCEを導出した。
さらに、単調性や公正コイン独立性などの追加公理により、標準的なOCEやエントロピーリスク尺度を特徴付けた。
papers.reason_ja: リスク尺度の公理的基礎付けに関心がある研究者に最適です。
papers.abstract: Optimized Certainty Equivalents (OCEs) are an important class of risk measures for optimization and risk management that includes the Mean--Variance criterion, Expected Shortfall, the Entropic Risk Measure, and expectation. Despite their importance, economic axioms have not characterized OCEs. We propose a new axiom called Fair-Coin Compensation, which characterizes OCEs together with Strong Risk Aversion and Normalization. We interpret Fair-Coin Compensation through the fair assignment of two losses by a coin toss: transfers between two participants can remove the additional risk created by the random assignment. Adding further axioms yields sharper characterizations. Monotonicity yields standard OCEs; Positive Homogeneity, together with Prudence, yields Expected Shortfall; and Fair-Coin Independence yields the Entropic Risk Measure. We also axiomatize the Mean--Variance criterion using our novel axiom of Equal-Mean Randomization, which states that random assignment of two losses with the same expected value does not produce a risk measure above the average of their risk measures.

papers.title: Shill-proof rules in object allocation problems with money
papers.title_ja: 金銭を伴う財配分問題における偽名入札耐性のあるルール
summary_ja: 財配分問題において、売り手が偽名入札（shill bidding）を用いて収益を操作するインセンティブを分析した。
偽名入札耐性、戦略的耐性、非賦課性を満たすルールの中で、収益が支配されないのは価格ベースの弱優先ルールであると示した。
この結果は、オンライン市場で採用される提示価格ルールが偽名入札耐性の観点から正当化されることを示唆する。
papers.reason_ja: メカニズムデザインと偽名入札耐性に興味がある方に推奨します。
papers.abstract: We consider the object allocation problem with money. The seller owns multiple units of an object and is solely interested in her revenue from an allocation. Each buyer can receive at most one unit of the object and has preferences over pairs consisting of consumption of the object and payments, which are not necessarily quasi-linear. We study the seller's incentives to increase her revenue by introducing false-name buyers, a practice commonly referred to as shill bidding. An (allocation) rule is shill-proof if the seller cannot increase the revenue by introducing false-name buyers. A rule is a price-based weak priority rule if there is a profile of prices such that buyers who are willing to receive the object at their own prices do so in descending order of price. We establish that a rule is revenue undominated among the class of rules satisfying shill-proofness, strategy-proofness, and non-imposition if and only if it is a price-based weak priority rule. Our result provides justification for the use of posted-price rules—widely adopted by online marketplaces, and internet auctions as ``buy-it-now'' auctions—over auction-type rules in terms of shill-proofness.

papers.title: An Enforcement Foundation for Constrained Equal Awards
papers.title_ja: 制約付き平等配分ルールの執行に関する基礎理論
summary_ja: 検証コストを伴う私的情報が申告される状況下でのルール選択問題を、標準的な請求問題の枠組みで分析した。
真実申告を弱支配戦略とするために必要な監査コストを最小化するルールとして、制約付き平等配分（CEA）を導出した。
CEAルールは、あらゆる事前分布の下で期待検証コストを最小化する唯一の許容可能なルールであることを示した。
papers.reason_ja: 配分ルールと監査メカニズムの理論的基礎に関心がある方に。
papers.abstract: Standard claims problems take claims as given. We ask how rule selection changes when a certified claim can be augmented by a privately known component that is costly to verify. In a binary environment, equal treatment of equals, claim boundedness, and efficiency impose a sharp lower bound on the gain from exaggeration and hence on the expected auditing needed for truthful reporting to be weakly dominant. The constrained equal awards (CEA) rule attains this bound at every report profile through a correlated audit policy. Conversely, every profilewise audit-minimal rule is CEA. The pointwise result also makes CEA the unique admissible rule that minimizes expected verification cost under every prior over true claims.

papers.title: Cognitive Constraints and Misspecification Concern
papers.title_ja: 認知的制約とモデルの誤指定に対する懸念
summary_ja: 認知的制約を持つエージェントが、モデルの誤指定を懸念しながら繰り返し意思決定を行う状況をモデル化した。
複雑さに対する制約により、統計的に劣る単純なモデルが長期的に選択され続ける可能性を明らかにした。
この制約は、モデルの誤りを露呈させるような選択を抑制し、誤ったモデルクラスを維持させる効果を持つ。
papers.reason_ja: 限定合理性や学習モデルに関心がある研究者におすすめです。
papers.abstract: We study repeated decision problems in which an agent has cognitive constraints and is concerned that her models might be misspecified. She first uses data to weight candidate models, subject to a cognitive-capacity constraint on the complexity she can process, and then she evaluates choices according to how well they perform under those models. More data need not overcome limited capacity: a statistically inferior but simpler model can remain relevant in the long run. When the constraint binds, evidence that favors models in proportion to their complexity can leave current behavior unchanged while still affecting later responses to data. This constraint eliminates cycles between risky and safe actions when simple models favor safety, and relaxing it can make risky play more attractive initially yet less frequent in the long run. It can also sustain misspecified model classes by suppressing choices that would reveal their errors.

papers.title: Distortion in Online Voting
papers.title_ja: オンライン投票における歪み（Distortion）
summary_ja: 計算社会選択とオンラインアルゴリズムを融合し、選択肢が逐次的に到着する環境下での投票ルールの歪みを分析した。
功利主義的枠組みと計量的枠組みの両方において、決定論的および確率的メカニズムの歪みの上界と下界を導出した。
オフラインの投票ルールをオンライン環境へ変換する手法を提案し、その性能限界を理論的に明らかにした。
papers.reason_ja: 計算社会選択とオンラインアルゴリズムの接点に関心がある方に。
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of distortion in online voting, a framework that bridges computational social choice and online algorithms. In contrast to the classical offline setting, where the full election instance is known in advance, we consider a dynamic environment where a fixed set of voters is present from the beginning, but alternatives arrive sequentially over time. Upon each arrival, a mechanism must immediately and irrevocably decide whether to retain the currently selected candidate or switch to the newly arriving one, operating solely on the partial ordinal rankings induced by the underlying cardinal preferences. We provide upper and lower bounds for deterministic and randomized mechanisms under two standard cardinal preference frameworks. Utilitarian framework: For deterministic mechanisms under adversarial arrival order, we establish an $Ω(mn)$ lower bound and give an matching online algorithm with distortion at most $\frac{2}{3}m(n+\frac{1}{4})$. For randomized rules, we introduce regularity, which allows any regular, order-independent offline randomized rule to be converted into an online rule with the same expected distortion. The Harmonic voting rule satisfies this property, yielding online distortion $O(\sqrt{m\log m})$. Metric framework: For deterministic mechanisms, maintaining an alternative within a $\varphi$-weighted uncovered set guarantees distortion $2+\sqrt{5}$. We show that matching-based offline rules achieving distortion $3$ cannot be directly implemented online. We establish a lower bound of $\sqrt{13}$, even with three alternatives, and a matching upper bound for three alternatives and any number of voters. For randomized mechanisms, regularity gives an online distortion of $3-\frac{2}{n}$ via Random Dictatorship.

papers.title: Proportional Representation for Almost-Solid Coalitions and the Proportional Veto Core for Rankings
papers.abstract: A proportional ranking should give groups of voters representation commensurate with their size at every prefix. Proportionality for solid coalitions (PSC) provides this guarantee to groups whose members rank the same set of candidates above all others. How much representation should a group receive when a few outside candidates disrupt that agreement? We extend the proportional veto core to rankings through candidatewise and setwise guarantees. We show that setwise veto protection is equivalent to robust Rank-PSC under reversal of both the voters' preferences and the collective ranking. Robust Rank-PSC extends representation guarantees to almost-solid coalitions at every prefix. Each distinct outside candidate that disrupts a coalition's agreement reduces its guaranteed representation by at most one, and this bound is tight. Using reverse-sequential variants of Ordered Phragmén and STV, we construct rankings satisfying robust Rank-PSC$+$ in polynomial time. This stronger axiom preserves the guarantee after deleting any suffix of the collective ranking and restricting voters' preferences to the remaining candidates. Verifying robust Rank-PSC is coNP-complete, whereas verifying robust Rank-PSC$+$ takes polynomial time. We also introduce Rank-Aligned PJR$+$, which requires the first $r$ candidates of the collective ranking to satisfy PJR$+$ when each voter approves their top $r$ candidates. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that meets this requirement simultaneously for every $r$. For fixed-size committees, the Expanding Approvals Rule guarantees Rank-PJR$+$ but can violate robust PSC regardless of how ties are broken or payments are assigned. We give a modification that satisfies both guarantees for any prescribed committee size.

papers.title: Reserve Systems in Dynamic Settings: Account Design and Inherited Rights
papers.abstract: Research on reserve systems mainly considers static settings, formulating and studying choice rules for a given allocation problem. Dynamic settings are different in that the problem is not given. Over time, more positions become available, and each time the institution must build the current problem from its past. We distinguish the ledger, which stores information about earlier allocations, the account, which transforms these data into the current problem, and the choice rule, which selects an outcome for that problem. The same choice rule can implement very different policies under different accounts. If each new batch is assigned while holding earlier recipients and their categories fixed, then as batches shrink, over-and-above, the most generous reserve policy we study, can select nearly the same recipients as minimum guarantee, the most conservative one. Cumulative implementation uses a different account, which reconsiders the categories of earlier recipients, and prevents this compression. We characterize it by resource-release invariance. With arrivals or changes in priorities, the ordinary choice rule might reject an earlier recipient whose appointment has to be honored. We introduce and characterize retain, reassign, and boost (RRB) choice rules, under which every incumbent retains her appointment and can have her category changed. Combining RRB with individual-proposing deferred acceptance gives a strategy-proof mechanism under which each incumbent keeps her appointment or receives one she prefers. Applications include waiting lists in school and university admissions, public recruitment, and court-ordered corrections.

papers.title: Computing EF1 Allocations with Few Value Queries
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that allocates $m$ indivisible goods among $n$ agents with nonnegative additive valuations using $O(n^5\log^2 m)$ value queries and guarantees envy-freeness up to one good (EF1). Concurrent work of Lin, Liu, Tao, and Zhou achieves $O(n^8\log m)$ comparison queries, attaining the optimal $O(\log m)$ dependence on $m$ for fixed $n$. Each comparison query can be simulated using two value queries, so their bound also holds for value queries. Our contributions are a much simpler algorithm and proofs, and polynomial-time computation.

papers.title: Biseparable representations of the Certainty Equivalents
On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination
papers.abstract: The envy cycle elimination (ECE) algorithm is a fundamental algorithm for the fair allocation of indivisible goods, guaranteeing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good under arbitrary monotone utilities. We show that the ECE algorithm can be implemented in $O(nm)$ time for $n$ agents and $m$ goods, and establish the tightness of this bound.

papers.title: Temporal Fair Division: Simultaneous Guarantees for Goods and Chores
papers.abstract: We study temporal fair division of indivisible items in both the goods and chores settings, with $n \ge 2$ agents and nonnegative additive values or costs. Items arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably. The arrival order and all agents' values or costs are known in advance, and the cumulative allocation must satisfy the fairness requirements after each arrival. For goods, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that simultaneously achieves exact temporal proportionality up to one item (TPROP1), a $1/n$ approximation to temporal maximin share (TMMS), and a $1/(n-1)$ approximation to temporal envy-freeness up to one item (TEF1). The TMMS factor is optimal. For chores, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that simultaneously achieves exact TPROP1 and a $2-1/n$ approximation to TMMS. Classical scheduling lower bounds based on fixed sequences carry over to chores TMMS, establishing the optimality of this factor for $n=2,3$. For every $n \ge 2$, we further show that $2-1/n$ is the optimal TMMS factor subject to exact TPROP1. For every fixed $n \ge 3$ and every finite $β\ge 1$, we construct an instance of chores admitting no $β$-TEF1 allocation.

papers.title: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division for Chores
papers.abstract: We study the fair division of indivisible chores that must be assigned in a prescribed order. The complete instance is known in advance, but assignments cannot be changed. Temporal envy-freeness up to one chore (TEF1) requires envy-freeness up to one chore after every arrival. For goods, TEF1 allocations need not exist, and deciding whether one exists is NP-hard. For chores, Elkind et al. (AAMAS 2025) showed that TEF1 allocations exist for two agents, but left open whether they always exist, conjecturing that they do not, and whether deciding their existence is hard. We resolve both questions, confirming the conjecture in a strong form: for every $n\ge3$ and every finite factor, some $n$-agent instance admits no allocation satisfying TEF1 even up to that factor. This holds even when all agents have the same multiset of individual chore costs, with nine chores sufficing for three agents. Deciding TEF1 existence is NP-complete for every fixed $n\ge3$, even when all costs lie within a factor $1+2^{-m}$ of one another, where $m$ is the number of chores. Instances without TEF1 allocations exist arbitrarily close to the uniform cost matrix with $O(n\log n)$ chores, and just nineteen for three agents. We then relate fairness to social cost. Even when a TEF1 allocation is supplied, minimizing social cost subject to TEF1 admits no polynomial-time approximation within any factor polynomial in the number of chores unless P$=$NP, already for three agents with strictly positive normalized costs. In contrast, for every fixed number of agents, we give an FPTAS for the optimal temporal EF1 factor, the smallest factor up to which TEF1 can be satisfied, whose output has social cost no larger than that of the cheapest allocation attaining this factor. Thus a slight relaxation of fairness permits a social-cost guarantee that, unless P$=$NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can provide under exact TEF1.

papers.title: Weighted Proportional Toll Sharing on General Highway Networks
papers.abstract: We extend the Segments Equal Sharing (SES) method of \citet{wu2024} from line highways to general highway networks, including networks with cycles. The input is an exogenously specified profile of route flows. We introduce the Weighted Proportional Sharing (WPS) method, which distributes each route's mileage revenue in proportion to weighted segment lengths and its fixed-surcharge revenue in proportion to positive segment surcharges. Route SES is recovered under homogeneous weights within each revenue component. We show that WPS is the sum of two weighted Shapley allocations and that the underlying route games extend the dividend and Shapley representation of linear SES. Two axiomatic characterizations identify WPS. The first uses additivity and proportional treatment of segments used on every positive-revenue route. The second combines sub-highway efficiency and weighted average balanced contributions under a route cancellation rule. We also extend Segments Proportional Sharing to general networks, identify it with the $τ$ value of the corresponding route game, and characterize it axiomatically. For Segments Compensated Sharing we characterize a weighted average tree allocation by consistency across rooted branch settlements and averaging under a specified root lottery. A cyclic example shows that different route splits can change the allocation even when origin--destination volumes and aggregate toll revenue are held fixed.

papers.title: Path-Independent Deleveraging Rules
papers.abstract: We characterise path-independent auto-deleveraging (ADL) rules as an extended log-exponential family. Immunity to account splitting, merging and reopening further restrict the class. Homogeneity (essentially) restricts the class to a one-parameter family ordered by both fairness and platform risk. Its split-proof members continuously interpolate between proportional division and water-filling. Among these rules, decreasing the parameter reduces risk at the cost of increasing inequality in how accounts are treated. This suggests selecting the parameter through an ex-ante calibration to a risk bound on historical data to choose a maximally fair rule subject to that bound. A counterfactual replay of Hyperliquid's ADL episode on 10 October 2025 finds that a range of intermediate parameters significantly improves on the observed allocation in both burden dispersion and subsequent risk statistics.

papers.title: Moral Inversion: Expressive Payoffs and the Reliability of Consensus
papers.abstract: Moral inversion is a public consensus on an account that falsely reverses responsibility for a harm. We study how expressive payoffs affect its emergence in a sequential social-learning model. A larger payoff makes an account more attractive to endorse, but also makes each endorsement of that account weaker evidence in its favor. We show that under a single-peakedness condition on private beliefs a larger payoff both increases the probability of an incorrect consensus on the favored account and reduces its reliability. Without this condition, both comparisons can reverse, and the informativeness of the public record can strictly improve in the Blackwell order. Finally, we show that a sufficiently large increase in the expressive payoff nevertheless restores the benchmark comparative statics.

papers.title: Expanding and Evaluating the Applicability of Safe Pareto Improvements
papers.abstract: Even when players can make credible joint commitments in games, disagreement about the game's default outcome (e.g., about equilibrium selection) can prevent them from agreeing on any particular payoff profile. We study safe Pareto improvements (SPIs): commitments that sidestep this obstacle by inducing a new game that is isomorphic to the original (after iteratively removing strictly dominated actions) but entrywise Pareto better. We do so by constructing token games: cheap-talk games rendered meaningful by commitments to take payoff-relevant actions (in prior work, strategies in the original game) as a function of the token outcome. Since these token games preserve the original game's strategic structure, players should expect them to be played isomorphically and hence agree that they Pareto improve on the original. In this work, we study token game SPIs under three additional commitment abilities: (1) burning utility, (2) transferring utility between players, and (3) transferring utility with an outside party conditional on the token outcome (e.g., via insurance-like contracts). We characterize when SPIs exist in each case and give efficient algorithms for optimizing over them. Finally, we propose evaluating SPI frameworks by how often they enable SPIs in randomly generated games. In such experiments, our methods substantially outperform prior work.

papers.title: Moral AI and the Erosion of Its Own Demand
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of human preference frequencies and AI adoption when individuals can choose between a moral AI that rules out defection and an unconstrained AI that preserves discretion. By allowing users to commit to cooperation, moral AI can sustain cooperation even when cooperative preferences are too scarce to do so on their own. But this success has a cost. By turning otherwise dormant cooperative preferences into committed behavior, moral AI exposes its users to exploitation by selfish individuals, causing the population share of conditional cooperators to decline under evolutionary selection. As conditional cooperators become less prevalent, equilibrium adoption eventually converges to zero. Moral AI can therefore be self-liquidating. For initial shares between the moral-AI adoption cutoff and the threshold for cooperation without AI, moral AI generates cooperation while lowering the limiting share of conditional cooperators. Adoption ultimately vanishes, leaving a lower share of the preference type that initially sustained demand for commitment.

papers.title: Ordinal Hegselmann-Krause Systems
papers.abstract: We study opinion formation in the popular Hegselmann-Krause model when agents replace the traditional averaging update by a median update or more general ordinal aggregation methods. We analyze the convergence properties of synchronous and asynchronous dynamics. For asynchronous dynamics, we show that every HKS with a $1$-Lipschitz ordinal aggregation function converges in worst-case time $\mathcal{O}(n^4)$. For the special case of median aggregation and for the family of $k\textsf{-large}$ aggregation functions, in which agents select the $k$-th largest opinion in their neighborhood, we obtain sharper bounds of $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$. For general ordinal aggregation, some sequence of $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ updates reaches an equilibrium from every initial state. Nevertheless, other update sequences may cycle, and uniform random activation can require exponentially many updates with overwhelming probability. For synchronous dynamics, we obtain a tight characterization. Ordinal aggregation functions satisfying the $1$-Lipschitz condition are shown to guarantee convergence in linear time. This result applies to many natural examples such as minimum, maximum, median, and $k\textsf{-large}$ functions. When the Lipschitz condition is violated, there exist instances in which synchronous dynamics do not converge at all.

papers.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors
papers.abstract: We study data-sharing among firms competing in the same market through the quality of their predictive models. We model firms' profit through two main components, precision and market share, where the former depends on the firm's own number of datapoints and the latter depends on the endowments of all firms. We characterize Pareto-optimal contracts as those in which at least one firm receives all of the other firms' datapoints. We then propose a parametric family of data-sharing contracts and show that, under any of them, the relative market shares of all firms remain constant, eliminating the negative effect of sharing data with competitors and equalizing all firms' gains relative to the no-sharing scenario. We further show that one contract within this family satisfies both Pareto-optimality and strategyproofness against firms attempting to under-declare the size of their initial endowment. Finally, using a real-world dataset, we empirically test the gain in profit for all firms under the contract described above, and show that data-sharing is particularly beneficial when the machine learning task is harder or when firms' initial endowments are closer to homogeneous.

papers.title: Two is better than one: optimizing binary rating scales for online platforms
papers.abstract: Online platforms often struggle with inflated, uninformative user ratings. This issue can be mitigated by better design of the data collection mechanism, for example through changing the phrasing of user questions. Previous work optimizes a single rating scale to best distinguish the inherent qualities of items under binary feedback. In this paper, we demonstrate the power of utilizing different rating scales for different users. First, we show that a designer can always split a single rating scale into two to improve item rankings. Next, we formally characterize the optimal design of multiple scales as a series of 0-1 step functions whose threshold values are evenly spaced. Finally, we consider an adaptive model where subsequent rating scales can depend on the responses from previous users and items are ranked by their full sequence of responses, and show that adaptivity leads to exponentially greater distinguishing power. All in all, our theoretical results show that using multiple rating scales significantly improves item rankings on platforms.

papers.title: Folk Theorems for Social Learning
papers.abstract: We study repeated games with purely informational externalities. Each player observes a single conditionally independent signal and then repeatedly takes publicly observed actions to maximize their expected discounted payoff, which depends only on the state and their own action. We show that, when there are sufficiently many players and they are sufficiently patient, there exist equilibria where information is aggregated: the players' payoffs approximate the full-information payoff. This holds even if actions are uninformative under myopic play. Conversely, even if myopic play reveals the state, there also exist equilibria where information is not aggregated: payoffs approximate those under autarky. Our results speak to the range of possible outcomes of social learning games with forward-looking agents.

papers.title: The Optimal Competitive Ratio for Subadditive Online Combinatorial Auctions is Less Than 1/2
papers.abstract: We construct a four-buyer online combinatorial auction with independent subadditive valuations and a fixed, known arrival order in which every online rule earns strictly less than $1/2$ of the expected offline optimum. A common partition, revealed at the third arrival, gives the first three buyers one unit of welfare per item. If the rule uses three distinct partitions, either an item allocated early contributes zero or the fourth buyer's expected value for the remaining bundle is one less than its size. We compute the optimal online and offline welfare exactly and show that a $1/2$ guarantee always holds with at most three buyers.

papers.title: Nash implementation of dynamic matching rules
Sequential Contract Design for Budgeted Crowdsourcing
papers.abstract: A principal wishes to crowdsource a collection of tasks under a fixed compensation budget. The quality of a task's outcome is stochastic and depends on the worker's effort level. Since this effort is unobservable, the principal offers contracts to workers specifying their compensation for each possible outcome. The principal offers these contracts sequentially, using previously observed outcomes and payments to decide whom to approach next and what contract to offer. The objective is to maximize the expected value of the work produced while ensuring that total payments never exceed the budget, regardless of the realized outcomes. Contract design must therefore account both for a worker's incentives and for the budget available to incentivize others. For valuations that are additive across tasks, we characterize how the approximability of the optimal adaptive policy depends on the numbers of workers, effort levels, and outcomes. Polynomial-time constant-factor approximation is possible whenever the number of workers, effort levels per worker, or outcomes per task is constant, but impossible in general when all three are unrestricted, unless $P=NP$. We obtain tight guarantees for every fixed number of workers, establish computational hardness even in restricted settings, and obtain exact algorithms and approximation schemes in more structured settings. We also investigate simple contract structures, demonstrating both the benefits of adapting contracts to previous outcomes and the limitations of local contract rules, while identifying conditions under which a local policy achieves a constant-factor guarantee. Finally, we extend our analysis beyond additive valuations, obtaining constant-factor approximations for monotone submodular valuations with binary outcomes, including guarantees against a stronger full-knowledge benchmark under additional assumptions.
